newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: FOCUS - Dutch Vendex to buy French temp agency BIS.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Dutch Vendex to buy French temp agency BIS.

text.p: Dutch retail and business services group Vendex said on Monday it planned a 2.5 billion franc ($475 million) takeover of French temporary employment agency BIS, creating a firm with a more pan-European focus.
Analysts welcomed the deal, saying it fitted well with the Dutch company's corporate strategy, and predicted growth in the French temporary employment market in coming years.
In Amsterdam, Vendex shares soared more than 10 percent to 84.50 guilders before slipping back to 81.90, still up 5.10 guilders, by early afternoon.

"Vendex is aiming for wider European coverage for temporary work and as such it is a good step. It looks like a good price they are willing to pay for BIS," said Keith Wills, analyst at London brokerage Goldman Sachs.
Analysts were also positive over plans to spin off Vendex's business services division and seek a separate listing for it.

"Vendex consists of three different divisions at the moment and the spin-off will make things clearer. It will give investors a clearer idea about valuation measures such as price-earnings ratios," said Peter Wortel at Delta Lloyd Bank.
"The spin-off makes it easier to understand the vehicle... there was no obvious synergy between retail and business services," Wills added.
The acquisition will more than double annual turnover of Vendex's business services division to more than six billion guilders ($3.4 billion).
It will create Europe's third largest temporary employment agency and the continent's second biggest in commercial cleaning.

Vendex said it had agreed to pay 490 francs per share for a 60 percent stake in BIS held by the family of its founder, Laurent Negro, who died last month. It will bid the same price for the remaining shares listed on the Paris bourse.
BIS shares are expected to resume trading on Tuesday, having been suspended on December 30 at 533 francs.

A BIS spokeswoman said the company expected a negative impact from the sale of some assets and this, combined with a forecast drop in 1996 earnings, explained the difference between the closing share price and Vendex's offer.
Vendex said its bid would be paid in cash from existing credit lines and would have a moderately positive effect on its earnings per share in the 1997/98 financial year.
BIS, France's third largest temporary help agency after Adecco and Manpower, made an operating profit of 141 million guilders on a turnover of some three billion in 1995.
Vendex derived 1.9 billion guilders of its 1995/96 turnover of 11.3 billion guilders ($6.4 billion) from the temporary work sector.
Its Vedior temp unit is mainly active in the Benelux countries but already ranks fifth in France and also operates in Spain and Germany. ($1=5.288 French Franc) ($1=1.757 Guilder)
